_about: What each route means to a visitor, read by k6 and the analyser. timeout_ms is the site's own timeout and must match public/home.js and public/signup.js (null = the site has none). on_failure says what a visitor does when the request fails or runs out of patience (patience_seconds in load-tests/test-config.json): "left" = leaves the site, "degraded" = carries on with a fallback. shown_on is the page address where a visitor sees this route.

GET /.while_slow: the page takes longer to appear

GET /api/rates.powers: Savings rate cards on the homepage
GET /api/rates.fallback: the cards show "Couldn't load rates right now."

GET /signup.while_slow: the page takes longer to appear
GET /signup.fallback: a blank loading tab or the browser's own error page (the site has no fallback of its own here)

POST /api/signup.powers: Submitting an email to create an account
POST /api/signup.fallback: after 3 seconds: "We couldn't confirm your sign-up. Check your inbox, or try again in a moment." If the connection fails: "We couldn't save your details just now. Nothing was submitted, please try again in a moment."
POST /api/signup.impact_if_failed: A person who wanted to open an account couldn't. For a bank this also costs trust.
